mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically each of the last four weeks (-23.7 to -20.3). This autoregressive momentum reflects a steady, gradual recovery in discretionary mobility that is likely to persist for the near term absent a shock, producing a continued upward trajectory over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is equal to or lower than its last-28-day mean despite the four-week run of weekly gains.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved by more than 5 points over the trailing two weeks (-17.7 to -10.9). Once workplace attendance crosses this recovery threshold, commute-linked lunchtime and after-work retail trips increase, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 points over the trailing two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -17.7 to -10.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following a greater-than-5-point WORKPLACES improvement in more than half of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals a coordinated return to out-of-home routine (commuting plus workplace attendance). When both series improve simultaneously week-on-week, the compounded increase in daily out-of-home time raises incidental retail and recreation visits more than either series alone would predict, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not exceed its last-28-day mean even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rose concurrently across the snapshot weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 14.0 to 11.7 over four weeks, indicating people are spending relatively less time confined at home. In a regime where social distancing is being eased rather than tightened, this decline in home-bound behavior is a direct substitute for increased discretionary outings, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 14.0 to 11.7 across the four snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks even as RESIDENTIAL continues to decline, indicating the substitution mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week jump in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (as seen from -7.1 to -4.3-ish range with volatility) can reflect anticipatory stockpiling ahead of an expected tightening of public health restrictions. When such a jump exceeds 5 points in a single week, it signals households are pre-positioning for reduced mobility, which precedes a broader pullback in discretionary RETAIL_REC visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fluctuated between -7.1 and -4.3 across the snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week following a greater-than-5-point single-week jump in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: The non-monotonic, oscillating pattern in PARKS (-10.6, -9.3, -12.6, -8.3) across the four weeks reflects transient weekend or short-holiday effects rather than a sustained structural shift in outdoor activity. Because these fluctuations are noise rather than trend, any short-term co-movement with RETAIL_REC is expected to mean-revert within one week rather than compound into a sustained directional move.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS oscillated non-monotonically across all four snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues trending in the same direction as the most recent PARKS fluctuation for more than one additional week, contradicting the mean-reversion assumption.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has been recovering steadily (-30.9 to -24.7), but if this recovery reverses with a drop of more than 5 points in a single week, it would indicate newly imposed restrictions on movement (e.g., tightened border or gathering controls). Under a tightening-restrictions regime, such a reversal in TRANSIT leads to a corresponding decline in RETAIL_REC within two weeks as discretionary trips are curtailed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 5 points week-on-week after a prior multi-week recovery
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved in each of the last three weeks before the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks following a greater-than-5-point single-week reversal in TRANSIT's recovery trend.

This combined reallocation effect is stronger than either series alone in predicting increased ancillary retail and recreation trips, since commuting and reduced home-confinement together compound discretionary outing opportunities over a four-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell while WORKPLACES rose concurrently across all four snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not exceed its last-28-day mean despite concurrent RESIDENTIAL decline and WORKPLACES increase across the snapshot period.
